questions.text: When setting up a debt snapshot, what is the recommended four-column format for organizing your debt information?
options: Creditor, Account Number, Due Date, and Principal Paid
Creditor, Balance (TT$), Interest Rate (APR %), and Minimum Monthly Payment (TT$)
Creditor, Original Balance, Collateral Type, and Credit Score
Creditor, Monthly Salary, Monthly Expenses, and Net Savings
questions.explanation: Lesson 1 specifies creating a table with columns for Creditor, Balance (TT$), Interest Rate (APR %), and Minimum Monthly Payment (TT$).

questions.text: True or false: The snowball method prioritizes paying off the debt with the highest interest rate first to minimize total interest paid over time.
questions.explanation: The snowball method starts with the smallest balance to secure quick wins, whereas the avalanche method targets the highest interest rate first.

questions.text: When negotiating restructured repayment terms with a lender, what key step should you always take before leaving the branch?
options: Pay off the entire loan principal immediately
Secure your newly agreed terms in writing
Sign an agreement for a new high-interest credit card
questions.explanation: Lesson 3 instructs borrowers to never leave the branch without securing their newly agreed terms in writing.

questions.text: True or false: Consolidating multiple debts into a single lower monthly payment over an extended repayment term will always reduce the total cash amount of interest paid.
questions.explanation: Lesson 3 notes that extending debt over a longer term often increases the overall total dollar amount of interest paid over the life of the contract.
